analysis: Examined two base-side text units (lines 15249-17286) of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json. They contain gemma-4-26b and gemma-4-26b-8bit test-vector cases (tool_call_arguments_bridge, tool_function_extra_keys, tools, unicode, assistant_harmony_framing, and others) with request_body, provider_body, template_input, plan (prompt_contract_id, block_boundaries, chain hashes) and token_ids. The patch excerpt (truncated) shows head changes elsewhere in the file: added additional_context {enable_thinking:false}, changed prompt_token_count 803 to 767, and altered chain hashes and token IDs. Changed ranges in the supplied range map sit around lines 3020-4003, 43739+, 52354+, which are not in the supplied base units, so the changes themselves were not directly visible here. This is a static golden-vector fixture, not executable code. It has no auth, attestation, key handling, encryption or billing logic, and no secrets (the content is synthetic prompts and token IDs). Relevant threat context is T-041, the prefix-cache oracle, since chain_hash and block_boundaries feed cache-key derivation. The fixture changes only test expectations, so no new attack surface or regression is visible. Remaining integration question: whether the head fixture's updated chain hashes, prompt_contract_id and additional_context match the Swift/Go prompt-rendering code. That is a correctness and cache-consistency concern rather than a demonstrated security issue, and the producing code is outside the supplied evidence. Another reviewer should check that the thinking-disabled context does not alter cache-scoping or cross-tenant sharing semantics.
